content:
watchOS 27 is set to launch later this month, and Apple Watch users may notice that some features work a little differently. The upcoming software update removes three features that users may miss after updating.

Apple Watch Walkie-Talkie App Removed

First up is the removal of the Walkie-Talkie feature, an Apple instant voice communication app that only works between Apple Watches.

Personally, Walkie-Talkie never really appealed to me, especially with the yellow app icon displayed on the watch face when enabled. Users who actually used the feature are already starting to miss it, and many more will notice its absence this month (and on new Apple Watches).

I don't think third-party apps can fully replicate what Apple offers with Walkie-Talkie on Apple Watch. However, a version that works on both iPhone and Apple Watch would probably be more popular.

Multitasking Shortcut Disappears

Next is the Digital Crown double-click multitasking gesture, which now does the same thing as a single click of the Digital Crown. I mentioned this previously in my watchOS 27 public beta preview, and again yesterday.

I don't know whether double-clicking the Digital Crown will become the multitasking gesture for watchOS. Being able to quickly switch between two apps, or between an app and the watch face, has always been very useful. I hope a solution returns in the future.

As for the double-click button shortcut, I think Apple Watch has a limited number of buttons, so double-clicking should correspond to some function, even if it's not multitasking. I now see this as two separate possible directions.

Dynamic App Grid Always Takes Priority

Finally, let's talk about what happens when you only single-click the Digital Crown.

Since watchOS 1 (then called Watch OS 1), clicking the Digital Crown from the watch face or within an app opens the full app launcher. The biggest change to this system before now was when Apple removed the design of centering the app grid and returning to the watch face on the first click.

watchOS 27 replaces it with a dynamic app grid: five smart-recommended apps, a Siri app, and an icon for the full app grid. You can tap the app grid icon, or scroll up on the Digital Crown to see the full app grid or list.

I understand this change. Apps on Apple Watch were never particularly popular to begin with. The new dynamic app grid offers larger tap targets and fewer icons to browse. It also puts the Siri app in a prominent position, a common theme across Apple's OS 27 family of updates.

If given the choice, I would probably turn off the dynamic app grid. As a default setting, I think it's okay, but it feels more cumbersome compared to going directly to the app launcher.

Regardless, any change takes a period of adjustment before it becomes second nature. That said, I've been using watchOS 27 since day one of beta 1 in June. For me, the loss of Walkie-Talkie isn't noticeable, losing the multitasking shortcut feels like only a temporary setback, and the dynamic app grid as a default is acceptable but a bit inconvenient for users who prioritize speed.

Of course, if the Explorer watch face could make a comeback, I'd accept all of the above changes. Removing features and changing how things work is to be expected, but deleting an Apple Watch face that users could already remove on their own is still puzzling.
